findings.title: Home-secret exposure from round 8 is fixed; residual is the blanket (allow file-read*) for non-home paths under --no-sandbox
findings.detail:
De-escalated from HIGH: the round-8 exposure is genuinely closed. c23ef9986 + b464cc197 add, after `(allow file-read*)` (:246), a home-wide deny built from pinLeadCredentialPaths([homedir()]) that denies file-read* under $HOME except require-not carve-outs for packageRoot, chromeRoot, qaRoot and the exact nodeExecutable (:250-256), plus a Crashpad carve-out that allows only file-read-metadata on the one literal host Crashpad directory (:260) while data reads there stay denied by the existing Google/Chrome credential deny. b464cc197 iterates over every resolved home alias (symlinked HOME) so a symlinked home cannot bypass the subtree match.

Verified empirically at this head. I built the real policy from the fresh dist (dist newer than src) and ran the pinned node 25.6.1 under `sandbox-exec -f` with it. Every path that read OK in round 8 is now denied: ~/.zprofile, ~/.zshenv, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.profile are READ-DENIED and STAT-DENIED; ~/Dev and ~/Library/Application Support are LIST-DENIED (all confirmed to exist outside the sandbox: 129 and 222 entries). Crashpad stat is allowed (intended metadata) while readdir is denied (intended). SBPL last-match-wins ordering is correct: home-deny and readDenials follow the broad allow, and the Crashpad metadata allow follows both. Ownership and file contents were never read; no secret was retained. The head's browser suite is 30/30 and the new root regression `final policy denies non-enumerated home secrets and limits Crashpad to directory metadata` passes.

Residual (why still MEDIUM, not resolved): `(allow file-read*)` still grants reads of everything OUTSIDE $HOME — /private/tmp (including other disposable activation roots), /var, /opt, /etc, /Library outside the enumerated credential roots. Under --no-sandbox a renderer compromise can read those. This is a much smaller and lower-value surface than the home secrets that were exposed in round 8 (no user dotfiles, no other-repo .env, no per-app Application Support), and Keychains/Apple system roots are already denied. It is a bounded, non-blocking hardening item, not a ship blocker: consider replacing the blanket allow with an allowlist of the roots Chrome and Node actually need (systemReadRoots at :39-51 plus packageRoot/chromeRoot/qaRoot) so non-home reads are closed too.

findings.title: Re-recording a step without re-supplying its prior mechanism finding orphans the append-only declaration and permanently blocks completion, with no diagnostic
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head; only browser-sandbox files changed since round 8. Declarations are append-only (:96-105) but applyPatrolJudgment removes only the re-recorded step's FINDING lines, and the canonical gate requires strict 1:1 pairing. Round 3 end-to-end: declare+finding gives complete:true; re-recording the step healthy gives complete:false; re-supplying the identical finding gives true again. A Lead that deems a declared defect a false positive can never close the tick, the wedged report persists on disk, and the failure is only a bare gates array. Surface a distinct reason, or add a retract path.

findings.title: The 30s per-request idle timer stays armed on CONNECT tunnels and WebSocket upgrades, silently tearing down the Lead's only egress path
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The 'connection' setTimeout(30_000, destroy) survives the hand-off to connect/upgrade listeners; a probe at 1s showed the tunnel closed at +1018ms with zero bytes. This proxy is the Lead model's only egress, so any HTTPS call or WebSocket idle for 30s or more dies with a bare FIN. Give tunnels a separate, larger idle budget or none.

findings.title: Artifact and model TMPDIR roots are mkdtemp'd directly inside the project git working tree and are not gitignored
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. `.flywheel-artifacts-*` and `.flywheel-model-*` are created under projectRoot and model TMPDIR points into the repo. Neither is gitignored, so the checkout stays dirty, `git add -A` stages scratch, crashes leak directories, and `git clean -xfd` deletes live roots. Gitignore both, or move them out of the tree.

findings.title: discord.message.attachments.send has only per-file caps and allows duplicate handles, so one 25 MiB artifact can drive a ~750 MiB peak on the Bridge
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Duplicate handles are allowed and there is no aggregate cap (250 MiB plus framing), so ten copies of one 25 MiB handle are buffered roughly three times per side. That can never succeed against Discord's 25 MiB limit — it is pure allocation in the shared Bridge. Cap the total size and reject duplicate handles.

findings.title: assertActivationCurrent does two full projects.json parses plus a ps(1) fork, and handlers call it several times per capability request
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Each call re-parses projects.json twice and forks ps, and handlers repeat it per request. This is an efficiency advisory (about 54 ms/request idle with the probe mocked). Memoize one parsed snapshot per request.

findings.title: scoped() rewrites ANY authorizeLabels throw into ScopeDenied, and linear.issue.search then silently drops that issue with no truncation signal
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The catch-all turns transient registry-read and probe errors into ScopeDenied, which the search loop skips, so issues silently vanish from results that carry no truncation flag. Deny-side only. Signal real scope denial explicitly and let other errors propagate.

findings.title: verifyBrowserHostIdentity's sourceModes/warnings output is computed then thrown away, and the ancestor-writability check that is enforced excludes chromeRoot
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The verification output (sourceModes, chrome_version_drift) is discarded, and the non-sticky writable-ancestor rejection covers only packageRoot, although /Applications is drwxrwxr-x and not sticky. That leaves the codesign-then-exec window open for the now no-sandbox Chrome. Enforce the output or remove it.

findings.title: Inherited from main #1203: 'off preserves ledger bytes' runs at the 5s default timeout and failed in 2 of 4 runs
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The test is byte-identical to main and advances fake timers 8 days (about 34,560 ticks at a 20s interval) under a 5000ms budget. Measured 5312/5650 ms FAIL and 4856/4369 ms pass. Per-tick code matches main, so this is main's timing debt, but it can red this PR's exact-head teamlead shard.

findings.title: The legacy-guard regression test bypasses the MCP SDK, so its CR/LF assertions do not reflect the production rejection path
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. McpServer is mocked (:28-40). The real SDK rejects CR/LF with -32602 before the handler (verified in round 5). One un-mocked registration assertion would catch a future SDK or zod break.

findings.title: A malformed MECHANISM_DISPOSITION line raises a raw SyntaxError/TypeError instead of patrol_judgment_invalid, over-reporting a pre-write rejection as an ambiguous write
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The unguarded parse throws raw errors, which the Bridge records as unknown even though nothing was written. Not reachable from current writers; guard the parse.

findings.title: createLeadRuntimeDirectories is unused in production and its layout is structurally incompatible with LeadArtifactStore
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Referenced only by its own test, and its artifactRoot would fail LeadArtifactStore's dirname === projectRoot check. Delete it, or make it the single allocator.

findings.title: assertFeaturePushBranch is called without defaultBranch at both lower layers, so the defense-in-depth gates cannot catch a default-branch push
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Both inner calls omit defaultBranch. Currently unreachable: git.feature.push is unconditionally denied.

findings.title: assertLeadGithubPrBinding binds on (project_name, pr_number) only, never on the repo the write lands in
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The binding never compares repo identity, and PR numbers collide across repos. It cannot fire today; compare the repo to harden it.

findings.title: The browser capability hardcodes arm64, exact Homebrew node/libnode digests, /Applications/Google Chrome.app and a founder-specific gbrain baseline, with no platform precondition and an opaque failure
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. There is no platform check, the exact-path digest pins break on upgrade, and every failure is one opaque browser_sandbox_configuration_invalid. Add explicit preconditions with distinct errors.

findings.title: LEAD_DEPLOYMENT_ENTRIES omits several of the most security-relevant compiled modules from the deployment receipt
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Omits permission-profile.js, catalog.js, model-env.js, broker-socket.js, receipts.js, capability-home.js, browser-config.js (carrying --no-sandbox), the browser egress modules, patrol-schema2.js and most bridge capability modules. browser-sandbox.js IS listed, so the home-deny policy change is covered; extend to the rest or document the receipt's scope.

findings.title: discord.thread.reply's outbox idempotency key omits text and replyTo, so reusing an eventId wedges the second reply in unknown forever
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Reusing an eventId with new text produces a key conflict, a permanent unknown receipt and an undelivered reply. Fail-safe but mis-reported; add text and replyTo to the key.

findings.title: The plain-HTTP proxy response callback does not re-verify activation currency, unlike the CONNECT and upgrade paths
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. Plain-HTTP responses stream without the revocation re-check the CONNECT and upgrade paths perform. Bounded, since new requests are denied.
